name: Santa Catarina
summary_text: Direction: worse than national — the only Brazilian state to have enacted a statutory bathroom restriction, and the venue of a nationally decisive refusal. Lei 19.686 of 21 January 2026 requires every educational institution in the state — basic, fundamental, secondary, technical and higher — to provide bathrooms separately by sex, banning shared or unisex installation and use, with fines of up to R$10,000; a second bill approved 22 December 2025 extends the ban to state and municipal public administration bodies; a third, tabled October 2025, would restrict school and locker-room use to the sex recorded on the birth certificate — continued legislative escalation rather than a one-off. The nationally decisive case arose here: a trans woman was refused entry to the women's bathroom by staff at a Florianópolis shopping centre, urinated on herself in front of shoppers and had to take public transport home; on 6 June 2024 the Supreme Federal Tribunal rejected her appeal, leaving refusals lawful under ordinary private-premises rules. In the other direction, Florianópolis has a visible LGBTQ tourism scene with pride events and legal infrastructure accustomed to processing same-sex marriages and marker changes; nationwide legal rights are identical, so visitors see the same federal protections as elsewhere. Caveat: state violence statistics sit atop the country's nationally leading lethality and should be read partly as reporting density rather than as gender-specific exposure.

sources.claim_summary: Encyclopedia overview of LGBT rights in Brazil: the 2011 Supreme Federal Court stable-union ruling; nationwide same-sex marriage via National Council of Justice Resolution 175/2013 (binding on all civil registry offices); the June 2019 Supreme Federal Court decision making homophobia and transphobia punishable under the anti-racism statute (imprisonment 1-5 years plus loss of public office); and gender-marker changes by self-determination.

sources.title: Brazil | Outright International
sources.claim_summary: Outright International country profile (updated 2026): over 3,000 openly LGBTQ candidates ran in the 2024 municipal elections; gender markers changeable by self-determination and trans voters may register with their lived identity; a national intersex human-rights working group installed in December 2023 with recommendations published October 2025; the national LGBTI+ health technical committee reinstated September 2025; a Superior Court of Justice ruling letting nonbinary people amend civil registry; and a proposed National LGBTQIA+ Rights policy running alongside a conservative legislative surge in congress.

LGBTQ+ law-firm guide for expatriates considering relocation to Brazil: legal framework overview — the 2011 stable-union ruling, CNJ Resolution 175/2013, and the 2019 ruling treating homophobia and transphobia as crimes equivalent to racism (1-5 years plus loss of public office), plus property, inheritance and immigration treatment of same-sex spouses; major cities including Florianópolis are broadly welcoming with pride events and established legal infrastructure, smaller towns may show more social friction though legal rights are identical nationwide.
